origin: nfl-desk-3fb93d11 (PR 79), re-verified where this desk touched it
title: nfl.com publishes no spreads, totals or moneylines
detail: The league's official site carries no betting prices, and no operator publishes a public, machine-readable, timestamped price history. The price store therefore has empty MARKET_OPEN and MARKET_CLOSE rows for every market we originate, and gate G2 (price provenance) cannot pass for any strategy.
consequence: Closing-line value, ROI at a real price, and demotion triggers D1a, D1b and D1f are all unmeasurable today.
action: Capture an operator price page on a fixed schedule and record the raw snapshot with a UTC timestamp, or accept that no strategy can ever be certified.

origin: nfl-desk-3fb93d11 (PR 79), re-verified where this desk touched it
title: The pinned mirror lags the official results feed
detail: Of 137 official 2026 finals, the mirror agrees on 136 and disagrees on 0. 1 game (2026 Week 10, Commanders @ Giants, Thursday 12 November) is final on nfl.com but still unscored in the mirror.
consequence: Any desk that reads scores from the mirror is up to several days behind the official page.
action: Keep nfl.com as the results source of record and treat the mirror as a cross-check only, which is what this desk does.

origin: nfl-desk-3fb93d11 (PR 79), re-verified where this desk touched it
title: MODEL_CLOSE is not yet observed for any market
detail: The store records the desk's origination price. Its close-out price can only exist once the pipeline runs again closer to kickoff, so every MODEL_CLOSE row is empty in this build.
consequence: We cannot yet measure how far our own line moves between origination and kickoff.
action: Schedule the pipeline to re-run a few hours before kickoff and write a second MODEL row; the store already has the slot for it.

origin: nfl-desk-3fb93d11 (PR 79), re-verified where this desk touched it
title: The Week 11 official injury report is not published yet
detail: Requesting https://www.nfl.com/injuries/league/2026/reg11 returns the Week 10 report; the only week tabs offered are 1 through 10. The report the desk would need to price Week 11 does not exist.
consequence: Every Week 11 market is originated with no injury or replacement-depth adjustment, and the model line carries no deficiency term.
action: Re-run the pipeline once the league publishes the Week 11 report; the adjustment column is already wired and will populate automatically.

origin: nfl-desk-3fb93d11 (PR 79), re-verified where this desk touched it
title: Depth charts are one club short and one day old
detail: 31 of 32 clubs publish a readable depth chart. Houston publishes its chart only as a raster image, so it contributes no rows rather than a guessed set. The snapshot was taken 2026-11-13.
consequence: Houston's replacement depth is unknown, and any club that edited its chart after the snapshot is stale.
action: Re-fetch weekly and fail closed (blank plus flag) for clubs that do not publish machine-readable charts.

origin: nfl-desk-3fb93d11 (PR 79), re-verified where this desk touched it
title: Out players still shown as first string on the club's own chart
detail: Build check: of 14 players the official report lists as Out, 0 are still printed as the first-string starter on their club's published depth chart. The check runs on every rebuild.
consequence: A club chart can lag the league's injury report by days, so 'starter available' can be wrong in both directions.
action: Keep reporting the check; treat a non-zero count as a data-quality incident for that club.

origin: nfl-desk-3fb93d11 (PR 79), re-verified where this desk touched it
title: Every bet is graded at a flat -110
detail: The mirror carries no per-leg prices for the 2026 season, so each graded bet is scored at the standard -110 convention with a 52.38% break-even.
consequence: Real prices vary by side and by game; ROI figures are indicative, not a statement of what a bet would have paid.
action: Replace with captured operator prices as soon as any exist (F-01).

origin: nfl-desk-3fb93d11 (PR 79), re-verified where this desk touched it
title: No player-prop lines exist from any source in this repo
detail: Neither nfl.com nor the mirror publishes player-prop lines. The prop-combo family S9 therefore produced no graded bets, and gate G7 (correlation audit) cannot be satisfied for any parlay or prop combination.
consequence: Two of the three bet classes in the brief cannot be priced at all.
action: Source prop lines with timestamps, or keep S9 on the board as an explicit, unpriceable entry rather than deleting it.

origin: nfl-desk-3fb93d11 (PR 79), re-verified where this desk touched it
title: The totals model does not beat a naive league-average baseline
detail: Out-of-sample on 2026 weeks 5-10: totals MAE 11.0038 points against 11.0235 for simply predicting the league average total every game.
consequence: Half of the origination chain (the total) currently adds no forecast value, and the moneyline inherits that because it is derived from the side and the total.
action: Rebuild the totals model before trusting any total or moneyline we originate; see suggestion S-04.

origin: nfl-desk-3fb93d11 (PR 79), re-verified where this desk touched it
title: The certification universe is far smaller than gate G1 requires
detail: The official feed holds 137 games. After the walk-forward warm-up, each family produced between 4 and 51 graded bets on the certification board, against a 300-bet minimum.
consequence: Nothing on the certification board can be certified this season, whatever its hit rate.
action: Accumulate seasons of official results, or lower G1 explicitly and record the increased false-discovery risk in the decision log.

origin: nfl-desk-3fb93d11 (PR 79), re-verified where this desk touched it
title: Home-field advantage is not distinguishable from zero this season
detail: The margin model fits home-field advantage at 0.21315058982628904 points per game on 130 non-neutral 2026 games. Session 864d5668 measured +0.47 with a 95% interval of -1.81 to +2.75 on the same season; this build publishes the point estimate and does not compute an interval.
consequence: A rule that leans on home advantage is leaning on a number we cannot separate from noise.
action: Add a confidence interval to the home-field coefficient and prefer multi-season fits; see suggestion S-06.

origin: nfl-desk-3fb93d11 (PR 79), re-verified where this desk touched it
title: Most official injury rows carry no game status at retrieval
detail: The Week 10 report lists 326 players; only 25 carry a game status (14 Out, 11 Questionable). Game statuses are published later in the week.
consequence: The replacement-depth tracker can only use practice status for the other 301 players, so 'out' is under-counted early in the week.
action: Re-read the report on Friday and again on Saturday; the tracker keys off game status and will change as it fills in.

origin: nfl-desk-3fb93d11 (PR 79), re-verified where this desk touched it
title: Every correlation previously published in this repo is inadmissible
detail: The brief now requires correlations to come only from officially sourced numbers with n published. Prior desks computed theirs from the nflverse mirror. Those values are not deleted - they are moved to correlations_withheld.csv with their basis and reason.
consequence: The correlations published here are fewer and narrower than what the site showed before. That is the point of the rule.
action: Recompute from official inputs only, which is what this desk does.

origin: nfl-desk-3fb93d11 (PR 79), re-verified where this desk touched it
title: The aggregator reference line has no timestamp, so it is neither an opening nor a closing price
detail: The mirror supplies one line per game per market with no snapshot time. The store records it as MARKET_REFERENCE, never as MARKET_OPEN or MARKET_CLOSE.
consequence: Any 'we beat the line by X' statement computed against it could be measuring a stale early-week price.
action: Do not quote a CLV number against it; the desk uses it only as a difference column and says so on every page.

title: No official or operator price exists anywhere in reach
detail: nfl.com publishes schedules, scores, standings and injury reports, and no spread, total or moneyline on any page read this session. Sportsbook operator sites are outside the sandbox network allowlist (TLS failure on direct fetch; the page fetcher reaches nfl.com and club sites only). MARKET_OPEN and MARKET_CLOSE are therefore stored as empty snapshot rows for all 39 originated markets.
consequence: Gate G2 ('verified opening and closing price') cannot pass for any family, so no strategy can be certified. Every market line published by this desk is AGGREGATOR tier.
action: Decision needed: accept an aggregator price tier for research and label it everywhere (current default), or commission a licensed price feed. Do not certify anything until one of the two is chosen.

title: Aggregator price has no disclosed book, jurisdiction, quote time or close
detail: The nflverse schedules asset is the only price-bearing file reachable from this sandbox. Its own data dictionary documents the columns but discloses no sportsbook, jurisdiction or quote timestamp for spread_line / total_line / moneylines, and the release page shows only an asset timestamp.
consequence: Any ROI computed from these numbers is research-grade. It is never labelled 'realised return' and never certifies a strategy.
action: Keep at AGGREGATOR tier. Re-derive the moment a licensed source exists.

title: MODEL_CLOSE is not observable in a single capture
detail: A closing price requires a later observation than the origin snapshot. This desk has made exactly one model snapshot (2026-11-15T23:30Z), so MODEL_CLOSE rows exist with a flag and no value.
consequence: Closing-line value cannot be computed by this desk yet.
action: Add a second capture after Week 11 kickoff; the store already accepts appended rows.

title: Houston publishes its depth chart as an image
detail: houstontexans.com/team/depth-chart renders the entire chart as one image (static.clubs.nfl.com/.../texans/a5or0zowuo36y1txf4ly) under the heading 'Unofficial Depth Chart'. There are no player rows in the markup. It was not transcribed by eye.
consequence: Houston's replacement cascade is blank. Any team-level model that needs a Houston depth feature is blocked.
action: Obtain an authorised structured source (club data feed or a licensed provider). Flagged rather than guessed.

title: Six players are named Out while absent from their club's own chart
detail: WAS Lucas Patrick (C, Concussion), DET Kerby Joseph (S, Knee, DNP), KC Omarr Norman-Lott (DT, Knee, limited), GB Micah Parsons (LB, Knee/Illness, limited), GB Josh Whyle (TE, Concussion, DNP) and IND Luke Rhodes (LS, Hamstring, DNP) are all designated Out on the official Week 10 report but are not printed anywhere on that club's depth page.
consequence: For these six, the report names an unavailable player with no published rank, so the position he vacates cannot be identified from official sources and no replacement is named here.
action: Depth must be validated against the roster and transactions log per club before a replacement is asserted. Logged, not inferred.

title: The pinned mirror in the repository is older than the live asset
detail: The live nflverse games asset was republished 2026-11-15T23:16:40Z (sha256 37f4e8f364119ff28fe15a921a12d8fb6d0a401dc6cc3b044140e9fbdd8f57ca per the release page). The pinned copy in data/decision-desk/raw/games.csv.gz was not refreshed by this session and therefore may lag on the latest results.
consequence: Aggregator prices and mirror cross-checks use the pinned copy. Divergence is possible for the most recent games.
action: Refresh the pinned copy under its owner's scope, or cite the live asset hash everywhere. Not edited here because that path belongs to another session.

title: The Week 11 injury report URL still serves Week 10 - reconfirmed
detail: https://www.nfl.com/injuries/league/2026/reg11 returns a page whose title and heading both read 'Week 10 of the 2026 Season'. Re-checked this session at 23:24Z on 2026-11-15. This independently confirms the prior desk's flag F-04.
consequence: Week 11 markets are originated with no injury adjustment. Personnel features exist only for Week 10.
action: Nothing to fix in code; wait for the league to publish, then capture weekly. The scheduled capture must be idempotent so a served-stale page cannot overwrite a newer one.

title: Inherited register ranks disagree with the clubs' live charts for 6 players
detail: Comparing the inherited 2026-11-13 register against today's live pages for 11 clubs: Philadelphia prints Jonathan Greenard and Jalyx Hunt as CO-rank-1 at EDGE and Arnold Ebiketie and A.J. Epenesa at rank 2, while the inherited register has ranks 2/3 and 1 for those men; Philadelphia's DT TY Robinson is rank 2 after an empty cell where the inherited register has him rank 1; Seattle prints Cooper Kupp AND Rashid Shaheed in the same rank-1 cell, so Shaheed is rank 1, not 2.
consequence: Replacement depth is wrong for those rows if read from the inherited register rather than the live page.
action: This desk reads the live page and shows both values side by side on the depth page. The inherited desk should be re-run.

title: Nine players are on a live chart but missing from the inherited register
detail: Players printed today by the club but absent from the inherited 2026-11-13 register: BUF Keleki Latu (TE, 4th), DET Jackson Meeks (TE, 4th), DET Nick Whiteside (CB, 4th), GB Kaleb Johnson (RB, 4th), IND Pharaoh Brown (TE, 4th), IND Will Mallory (TE, 4th), KC Jake Briningstool (TE, 4th), NYG Thomas Fidone II (TE, 4th), SEA George Holani (RB, 4th). Separately, GB Coleman Owen and BUF Te'Cory Couch appear in the inherited register but not on today's page.
consequence: The inherited register silently truncates every 4th-string row. A four-deep deficiency matrix built on it would miss real depth.
action: This desk parses all published ranks including 4th. Clubs with 4-deep charts are the reason.

title: The personnel (availability) feature cannot be estimated on one week
detail: The availability differential was regressed on the Week 10 margin for the 9 Week 10 games with a final score: coefficient -1.89 points per extra unavailable player (standard error 2.26, n=9). The confidence interval spans zero by a wide margin.
consequence: No fixed points penalty for a missing starter is defensible from this sample, which is exactly why this desk ships an ablation rather than a penalty.
action: Extend the injury archive back several seasons (see the archive question Q-05) and re-estimate on a chronological holdout before the feature enters the model.

title: No inactive list and no snap counts are captured
detail: The official Week 10 report carries a game designation on 171 of 347 rows; 176 rows carry none. No official inactive list and no snap-count table were captured, so for any player not designated Out there is no official evidence he played, and no measured split between starter and backup exists.
consequence: A backup's replacement of a starter can be *published* but not *confirmed*. Depth cannot be modelled from playing time, and 'not listed' cannot be read as 'available'.
action: Capture the inactive list and snap counts weekly. Until then the replacement columns are labelled as published evidence, not confirmed participation.

title: The report's own designation reliability is unmeasured
detail: Of 347 Week 10 rows: 70 Out, 11 Doubtful, 90 Questionable, 176 with no designation. The play rate of a Questionable player is not published anywhere, and the official text gives no percentage.
consequence: Designation cannot be used as a numeric feature with a stipulated play probability.
action: Join several seasons of designations to inactive lists and measure play rates with confidence intervals first (question Q-06).

title: The prior desk's Week 10 row is a single game and its game links are week-level
detail: nfl-desk-3fb93d11/data/results_feed.csv held 137 rows: weeks 1-9 complete plus exactly one Week 10 game (WAS@NYG), because that capture happened while the other Week 10 games were still being played. Each row links to a week page rather than the game.
consequence: Citing that file for Week 10 gives a misleading picture of what was final.
action: This desk captures Week 10 itself (9 finals at capture time) and adds a per-game URL to every row, marked VERIFIED for Week 10 and CONSTRUCTED for weeks 1-9.

title: Eighteen games in the feed are absent from, or lag in, the pinned mirror
detail: Of 145 official finals in the feed, 127 are corroborated by the pinned mirror, 0 disagree, and 18 are absent from it. Absence is a mirror lag, not a contradiction, and is never counted as agreement.
consequence: The mirror cannot be used as a second source for the newest games.
action: Publish the 18 explicitly (see results page) and re-check after the mirror refreshes.

title: One chart is internally inconsistent
detail: The Green Bay chart lists Kitan Oladapo as rank 2 behind two different safeties in the same chart (behind Xavier McKinney at one S slot and Evan Williams at another). Philadelphia lists Jonathan Greenard as co-rank-1 at two different EDGE slots.
consequence: A player cannot back up two starting slots in one game; the chart is a publication artefact, not a lineup.
action: Stored verbatim with both rows. The replacement-cascade logic takes the next rank in the same group, so it cannot double-count a man across slots.

title: A kicker is absent from its own club's chart
detail: Baltimore's chart prints a 'K' row with no player at any rank. Every other special-teams row on that page is populated.
consequence: Special-teams depth for Baltimore is incomplete and no kicker is inferred.
action: Recorded blank. Not repaired from a news headline.

title: No player-prop price exists, so prop combinations cannot be graded
detail: Not one player-prop line exists in any source reachable from this sandbox. The same-family prop-combination strategy therefore has zero graded bets and its joint-probability gate cannot be evaluated.
consequence: The prop-combination leaderboard division is empty by construction, not by failure.
action: Blocked on a licensed prop feed. Do not synthesise prop prices.

title: Some listed players are not on any injured-reserve or report list at all
detail: Malik Willis (MIA) and Lamar Jackson (BAL) are on injured reserve per dated nfl.com headlines and appear nowhere in the Week 10 report. Puka Nacua appears in the Week 10 table with a blank game status while a dated headline says he is likely to be placed on IR.
consequence: 'Absent from the report' cannot be read as 'available', and a blank status cannot be read as 'cleared to play'.
action: The availability page carries an explicit reserve-list-evidence section. A blank designation is published as no designation, never as a level.

title: Eleven prior NFL desks answer overlapping slices of this brief
detail: nfl-strategy-lab, nfl-decision-desk, nfl-decision-desk-38a1fc27, nfl-decision-desk-e413f933, nfl-b34253a1, nfl-desk-26d4cafb, nfl-desk-864d5668, nfl-desk-d38e90c5, nfl-desk-3fb93d11, nfl-engine-39086ec8 and nfl-hub-28431d9c each publish their own leaderboard, gates and flags from their own snapshot. Three of them (d38e90c5, 3fb93d11, 853c0074) say in their own coordination entries that they answer the same price/results/signal-split gap.
consequence: There is no single authoritative leaderboard, and a reader cannot tell which desk's number is current.
action: This desk is additive and publishes a desk reconciliation page naming what each prior desk claims and which of its numbers this session re-verified. Consolidation remains the user's call.

title: Two capture-ledger counts were wrong (Week 11 slate said 14 games; injury capture said 254 rows)
detail: sources_captured.csv stated '14 games' for the Week 11 slate while the page lists 13 and the desk's own slate file carries 13, and stated '254 player rows' for Week 10 while the committed injuries_wk10.csv holds 347. Both were transcription errors in the NOTE, not on the official page.
consequence: A reader using the ledger instead of the data would mis-size the slate and the injury universe.
action: Both notes corrected in place with a CORRECTION LOGGED sentence; counts are now copied from the files, not typed.
